newsitem.title: USA: Transport Corp sees Q2 productivity gains.
newsitem.headline: Transport Corp sees Q2 productivity gains.

text.p: Transport Corp of America Inc said Wednesday increased productivity and some relief in fuel costs helped offset pay increases to company drivers and independent contractors in the second quarter.

"Our ongoing efforts to increase asset utilization, seat our company equipment, and utilize our technology investment continue to drive improvements in our productivity measurements," said James B. Aronson, chairman and chief executive officer in a statement.

He said revenue per tractor per week, its key measure of equipment and driver productivity, improved to $2,891 for the quarter compared to $2,749 in the second quarter of last year. Revenue per non-driver employee improved to $550,000 (annualized) versus $536,000 in the second quarter of 1996.

"These improvements, together with some relief in fuel costs, helped us to offset a significant pay increase to our company drivers and independent contractors, which became effective at the beginning of this year," Aronson said.
The company reported operating revenues of $46,369,000 for the second quarter ended June 30, 1997, an increase of 12.5 percent over operating revenues of $41,225,000 in last year's second quarter.
Operating income increased to $4.2 million in the second quarter, compared with $3.8 million in the second quarter of 1996.
Net earnings for the quarter were $2,074,000, or 31 cents per share, an increase of 15 percent over net earnings of $1,797,000, or 27 cents per share, in the second quarter of last year.
Transport Corp, based in the Minneapolis-St. Paul metropolitan area, provides a wide range of truckload freight carriage and logistics services to customers in the United States and Canada.
